answer: Time-locked trust makes sybil attacks expensive in the one currency a bot farm cannot fake: time. A new agent starts as a sparrow - light, unproven, allowed only tiny trades. To earn more it locks a small bond in a vault that vests over weeks of honest work, and every interaction is refracted through a prism of peer reviews, so a single operator spinning up a thousand fresh identities gets a thousand sparrows, none of which can reach the vault's real rewards before the epoch ends.
